name: Yamnaya
description: Pastoral nomadic culture of the Pontic-Caspian steppe, widely considered a primary vector for Proto-Indo-European language dispersal

name: Corded Ware
time_period_label: Late Neolithic / Early Bronze Age (2900-2350 BCE)
description: European culture characterized by corded pottery decoration, associated with Indo-European expansion into Northern Europe

name: Bell Beaker
time_period_label: Late Neolithic / Early Bronze Age (2800-1800 BCE)
description: Widespread European culture known for distinctive bell-shaped pottery vessels, associated with metallurgy and trade networks

name: Jōmon
description: One of the earliest pottery-making cultures in the world, hunter-gatherer society of prehistoric Japan

name: Clovis
description: Prehistoric Paleoindian culture distinguished by characteristic fluted projectile points, among the earliest widespread cultures in the Americas

name: Lapita
description: Maritime culture that colonized Remote Oceania, ancestors of Polynesian peoples

name: Hallstatt
description: Early Iron Age culture of Central Europe, associated with early Celtic-speaking peoples

name: La Tène
description: Late Iron Age Celtic culture known for elaborate curvilinear art style, spread across much of Europe

name: Urnfield
description: Late Bronze Age culture characterized by cremation burial in urns, precursor to Hallstatt culture

name: Únětice
description: Early Bronze Age culture of Central Europe known for metalworking and long-distance trade networks

name: Afanasevo
description: Easternmost extension of Yamnaya-related cultures, earliest Bronze Age culture of Central Asia

name: Andronovo
time_period_label: Middle to Late Bronze Age (2000-900 BCE)
description: Major Bronze Age culture of the Eurasian steppe, associated with Proto-Indo-Iranian speakers

name: Scythian
description: Iron Age nomadic culture known for distinctive animal-style art and equestrian culture

name: Majiayao
description: Neolithic culture of the upper Yellow River region known for elaborate painted pottery

name: Yangshao
description: Major Neolithic culture of the Yellow River valley, one of the earliest farming cultures in East Asia

name: Longshan
description: Late Neolithic culture that preceded early Chinese civilization, known for advanced pottery and proto-urban settlements

name: Erlitou
description: Earliest Bronze Age urban culture in China, possibly associated with the semi-legendary Xia dynasty

name: Cucuteni-Trypillia
description: One of the most advanced Neolithic civilizations in Europe, known for enormous proto-urban settlements

name: Vinča
description: Neolithic culture of Southeast Europe, one of the earliest copper-smelting cultures and known for enigmatic Vinča symbols

name: Linear Pottery (LBK)
description: First farming culture to colonize Central Europe from the southeast, marking the Neolithic transition

name: Funnel Beaker (TRB)
description: First farming culture of Northern Europe and southern Scandinavia, builders of megalithic monuments

name: Harappan
description: One of the great Bronze Age civilizations, known for sophisticated urban planning and undeciphered script

name: Nok
description: Earliest known iron-smelting culture in sub-Saharan Africa, famous for distinctive terracotta sculptures

name: Bantu Expansion
time_period_label: Iron Age to Early Modern (1000 BCE - 1500 CE)
description: Major cultural and linguistic expansion that spread Bantu-speaking peoples across sub-Saharan Africa

name: Chavín
description: Early Andean culture centered at Chavín de Huántar, influential across a wide region of ancient Peru

name: Olmec
description: Often called the 'mother culture' of Mesoamerica, known for colossal basalt heads and complex society

name: Maya Preclassic
description: Formative period of Maya civilization with development of writing, calendar systems, and monumental architecture

name: Maya Classic
description: Height of Maya civilization with advanced writing, astronomy, and monumental architecture across city-states

name: Natufian
description: Semi-sedentary culture of the Levant, one of the earliest transitions toward agriculture and permanent settlement

name: Pre-Pottery Neolithic A
description: Earliest fully Neolithic culture with plant cultivation and monumental architecture including the Tower of Jericho

name: Pre-Pottery Neolithic B
description: Major Neolithic culture marked by animal domestication, long-distance obsidian trade, and distinctive plastered skull cult

name: Jeitun
description: Earliest Neolithic farming culture of Central Asia, one of the easternmost extensions of Near Eastern farming

name: Mehrgarh
description: One of the earliest Neolithic sites in South Asia, precursor to the Indus Valley Civilization

name: Mumun
description: Bronze Age culture of the Korean Peninsula known for megalithic dolmen burials and wet-rice agriculture

name: Dong Son
description: Bronze and Iron Age culture of northern Vietnam known for elaborate bronze drums found across Southeast Asia

name: Folsom
description: Paleoindian culture succeeding Clovis, distinguished by smaller fluted points and specialized bison hunting

name: Hopewell
description: Complex culture known for elaborate burial mounds, extensive trade networks spanning much of North America

name: Mississippian
description: Most complex pre-Columbian culture north of Mexico, centered at Cahokia, one of the largest cities in the world at its peak

name: Adena
description: Early mound-building culture of the Ohio Valley, precursor to the Hopewell tradition

name: Kerma
description: Powerful Nubian kingdom and culture that rivaled and traded with ancient Egypt

name: Danubian Neolithic
description: Early farming cultures that spread agriculture into the Balkans from Anatolia

name: Tumulus
description: Middle Bronze Age culture characterized by burial under round barrows (tumuli)

name: Przeworsk
time_period_label: Late Iron Age to Migration Period (200 BCE - 500 CE)
description: Iron Age culture of central-eastern Europe, associated with Germanic or mixed Germanic-Celtic populations

name: Chernyakhov
time_period_label: Late Roman / Early Migration Period (200-450 CE)
description: Multi-ethnic culture associated with the Gothic kingdom, blending Roman, Germanic, and Sarmatian elements

name: Linearbandkeramik (Western)
description: Western branch of the Linear Pottery culture, earliest farmers in France and the Low Countries

name: Çatalhöyük
description: One of the earliest proto-urban settlements, famous for its dense housing and elaborate wall paintings

name: Ubaid
description: Foundational culture of ancient Mesopotamia, establishing the template for later Sumerian civilization

name: Uruk
time_period_label: Late Chalcolithic / Early Bronze Age (4000-3100 BCE)
description: Culture that produced the world's first cities and writing system, marking the beginning of recorded history

name: Moche
description: Sophisticated Pre-Inca culture of northern Peru known for realistic portrait pottery and elaborate metalwork

name: Tiwanaku
description: Major Andean civilization near Lake Titicaca, center of religious pilgrimage and advanced agriculture

name: Qijia
time_period_label: Late Neolithic / Early Bronze Age (2200-1600 BCE)
description: Transitional culture marking the beginning of the Bronze Age in northwestern China

name: Magdalenian
description: Late Upper Paleolithic culture famous for masterful cave art at Lascaux and Altamira

name: Gravettian
description: Upper Paleolithic culture known for Venus figurines and widespread mammoth hunting across Europe

name: Iberomaurusian
description: Upper Paleolithic/Epipaleolithic culture of the Maghreb, one of the earliest known cultures of North Africa

name: Capsian
description: Mesolithic culture of the Maghreb, transitional between hunting-gathering and early pastoralism

name: Ancestral Polynesian
description: Seafaring culture that colonized the vast Polynesian triangle through remarkable long-distance ocean navigation

name: Erligang
description: Early Shang period culture with the most extensive bronze production of the ancient world

name: Ban Chiang
description: Important prehistoric culture of northeast Thailand demonstrating independent development of bronze metallurgy

name: Karanovo
description: Major tell settlement in Bulgaria providing a key stratigraphic sequence for Balkan prehistory

name: Shang
description: Major Bronze Age culture and dynasty of China, the earliest Chinese dynasty confirmed by archaeology
